fault_judgment: The most likely fault is a mismatch between the DNN requested by the devices, plant-edge, and the DNN configured on the SMF, plant_edge. The exact name mismatch and the SMF's no-matching-configuration log directly account for the affected sessions failing while the other DNN remains available. Align the device subscription/request and the SMF DNN configuration, then verify session establishment.
excluded_causes: A general radio-access outage is inconsistent with successful registration and working office-data sessions. An authentication failure is inconsistent with the completed authentication procedure. A broad SMF outage is also less consistent with the successful office-data sessions and the explicit no-matching-DNN log entry.
evidence_analysis: Successful registration and authentication show that the devices can reach the access and registration procedures. The failure occurs when the requested DNN is resolved for session establishment. The UE requests plant-edge, while the SMF configuration contains plant_edge; the SMF log independently reports no matching DNN configuration. Normal office-data sessions show that session establishment is not failing for every DNN.
diagnostic_question: What is the most likely cause of the plant-edge session failures, and which alternatives are inconsistent with the observations?
symptom_description: Devices at the production site register successfully, but attempts to establish a data session for the plant-edge service fail. Sessions using the office-data service remain available.
configuration_observations: Authentication and registration complete successfully for the affected devices. Their session requests specify the DNN plant-edge. The SMF has a DNN profile named plant_edge but no profile named plant-edge, and its session logs report that no matching DNN configuration was found. The office-data DNN is configured and its sessions are established normally.
